audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch use byte-exact comparison for commitment deduplication to prevent hash collision attacks?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Deduplication in the C library's deduplicate_commitments uses memcmp on 48-byte commitment arrays (commitments_equal returns memcmp(a->bytes, b->bytes, BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT) == 0). This is a byte-exact comparison, not a hash-based one. The abstract domain for commitment equivalence is strict byte equality over all 48 bytes.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample is possible: two symbolic byte sequences C1 and C2 where C1 != C2 byte-for-byte will never satisfy commitments_equal, so no attacker-crafted pair of distinct commitment bytes can be deduplicated together incorrectly. Hash collision attacks are inapplicable since no hash function is involved in the deduplication path.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The deduplication is performed entirely within the C library after the Go wrapper copies commitments_bytes into the library's internal buffer. An attacker-controlled commitment byte sequence enters at the P2P boundary and is processed through VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> C verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch -> deduplicate_commitments.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: deduplicate_commitments uses strict byte equality (memcmp over 48 bytes). No hash collision vulnerability exists in this path. The property PROP-W5B14-7 is satisfied for byte-exact comparison.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: commitments_equal uses memcmp(a->bytes, b->bytes, BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT) — 48-byte exact comparison in c-kzg-4844 C library

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The deduplication algorithm uses byte-exact memcmp over all 48 bytes of the commitment. This is the strongest possible comparison for binary commitment bytes and is not susceptible to hash collision attacks. The implementation is correct.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No action required. The deduplication mechanism is sound.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) enforce unique commitments in its input list?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm's VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs builds the commitments slice with one entry per cell (possibly repeated for same blob across different columns). The C library allocates unique_commitments of size num_cells and calls deduplicate_commitments internally before weight aggregation.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The C library explicitly handles repeated commitments: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch allocates num_commitments = num_cells, then calls deduplicate_commitments to consolidate. The function is designed to accept and process repeated commitments — uniqueness is not a precondition of the API.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Prysm relies on the C library to deduplicate; this is the intended usage per the API design. The Go wrapper does not need to pre-deduplicate.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The C API for verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch explicitly accepts non-unique commitments and performs deduplication internally before weight aggregation. No precondition violation exists.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: deduplicate_commitments called in eip7594.c before any weight aggregation; Go layer passes commitments slice correctly

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No precondition violation exists. The C library accepts repeated commitments and deduplicates them internally. Prysm's usage pattern (one commitment per cell) is consistent with this API contract.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer craft commitment bytes that bypass deduplication and corrupt weight aggregation?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: An attacker submitting crafted commitment bytes would need either: (a) two byte sequences that are identical under memcmp but represent different EC points — impossible by definition; or (b) two byte sequences distinct under memcmp but representing the same EC point (non-canonical encoding) — these would pass as separate commitments in deduplication but bytes_to_kzg_commitment would validate encoding and reject invalid encodings.
state_anomalies_found: Theoretical: non-canonical BLS12-381 encodings could produce split weights, but are rejected by bytes_to_kzg_commitment EC validation

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: BLS12-381 G1 compressed point encoding is injective over valid curve points — each valid point has exactly one canonical byte representation. Invalid encodings trigger C_KZG_BADARGS from bytes_to_kzg_commitment, propagated as error through Go wrapper, handled as ErrInvalidKZGProof. No path allows crafted bytes to corrupt weight aggregation without being rejected.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker-supplied commitment bytes flow from P2P to C library; invalid encodings are caught by bytes_to_kzg_commitment during weight aggregation. The verification returns error (not false positive), causing peer rejection.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: BLS12-381 injectivity ensures byte-exact memcmp correctly deduplicates all valid commitments. Invalid encodings are rejected before weight aggregation can be corrupted. No successful canonicalization attack is possible.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: bytes_to_kzg_commitment EC point validation in C library; BLS12-381 G1 injectivity of canonical encoding

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: BLS12-381 G1 compressed point encoding is injective for valid curve points. Invalid encodings are rejected by bytes_to_kzg_commitment before corrupting weight aggregation. No successful canonicalization attack against deduplication is possible.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: What is the consensus impact if a validator node accepts a batch proof with incorrect deduplication?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: If deduplication were incorrect, weight aggregation would assign wrong r_powers to commitments, altering final_g1_sum in the pairing check. This would cause valid proofs to fail (liveness impact) but could not cause invalid proofs to pass (safety impact) due to discrete log hardness of the KZG pairing.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The pairing check soundness depends on discrete log hardness, not on deduplication correctness. Incorrect commitment aggregation could produce a wrong final_g1_sum but cannot be crafted to satisfy the pairing equation for an invalid proof. The failure mode is false negative (DoS), not false positive (safety bypass).

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Since the deduplication is correct (byte-exact memcmp), this theoretical impact path is not reachable. The liveness-not-safety failure mode makes this a DoS concern at most.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: KZG soundness: incorrect commitment deduplication cannot produce false positive verifications. Failure mode is at most liveness degradation. Since deduplication is correct, no actual impact exists.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: KZG pairing check soundness via discrete log hardness; correct byte-exact deduplication in C library

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Deduplication is correct, so no actual impact. Even hypothetically, incorrect deduplication causes liveness degradation (valid proofs fail), not consensus safety failure. Discrete log hardness prevents false positive verifications regardless of aggregation logic.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Are all commitment_indices validated to be within bounds of the deduplicated commitments array before array access?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The commitment_indices array is produced by deduplicate_commitments (not attacker-supplied). deduplicate_commitments invariant: indices_out[i] < new_count <= initial_count = num_cells. Arrays commitment_weights and commitments_g1 are of size new_count. Cell indices (column indices) bounded by two independent layers: Go VerifyDataColumnSidecar (sidecar.Index < 128) and C library (cell_indices[i] >= 128 -> BADARGS).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For OOB on commitment_weights[commitment_indices[i]], need commitment_indices[i] >= new_count. But deduplicate_commitments sets indices_out[i] = j where j < new_count, or indices_out[i] = new_count and then new_count++ immediately after. So indices_out[i] < new_count always. No OOB possible. For cell_indices: double-bounded by Go + C. No counterexample exists.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker cannot influence commitment_indices — derived internally by deduplicate_commitments. Attacker-controlled sidecar.Index validated < 128 before KZG verification. Both bounds checks are in place.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Three independent mechanisms prevent OOB: (1) peerdas.VerifyDataColumnSidecar validates sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns=128 (p2p_interface.go:37); (2) C library validates cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128 returns C_KZG_BADARGS; (3) deduplicate_commitments structural invariant ensures indices_out[i] < new_count by construction.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: p2p_interface.go:37 (sidecar.Index < 128); eip7594.c:840 (cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB); deduplicate_commitments invariant (indices_out[i] < new_count)

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Multiple layers of bounds validation prevent any out-of-bounds array access. commitment_indices is internally computed (not attacker-controlled), and both Go and C layers independently validate cell_indices bounds. No OOB vulnerability exists.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ModExp gas computed before memory allocation?

code_scope.resolution_error: EIP-7883 ModExp precompile gas computation is an EVM execution layer concern. No ModExp precompile code found in OffchainLabs/prysm@238d5c07df (consensus client only).

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Target repository is an Ethereum consensus client (beacon chain). ModExp precompile gas computation resides in execution layer clients (go-ethereum, Erigon, Reth, etc.). No relevant code exists in this repository.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Out-of-scope: EIP-7883 ModExp precompile is an execution layer EIP. OffchainLabs/prysm is a consensus client with no EVM execution code. This check applies to execution clients only.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Apply this check to go-ethereum, Reth, or other execution layer clients.
